To find the characteristic polynomial of a matrix, we need to compute the determinant of the matrix $A-\lambda I$, where $A$ is the given matrix, $\lambda$ is the eigenvalue we are solving for, and $I$ is the identity matrix of the same size as $A$.

First, we calculate the matrix $A-\lambda I$:
$$A-\lambda I = \left(
\begin{array}{ccc}
-4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14-\lambda \\
\end{array}
\right)$$

Now, we find the determinant of this matrix:
$$\text{det}(A-\lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)((10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda)-(-5)(4)) - (-13)((-9)(-14-\lambda)-12(4)) + 10((-9)(-5)-12(10-\lambda))$$
$$= (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 140 + 20) - (-13)(126+\lambda) + 10(45-12\lambda)$$
$$= (\lambda+4)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) - (-13)(\lambda+126) + 450-120\lambda$$
$$= \lambda^3 + 4\lambda^2 - 120\lambda + 4\lambda^2 + 16\lambda - 480 + 13\lambda + 1638 + 450 - 120\lambda$$
$$= \lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 121\lambda + 1638$$

Therefore, the characteristic polynomial of the matrix is $\boxed{\lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 121\lambda + 1638}$.
